entradas.text: ”Welcome to the Ministry of Defense, Mr. President. Let's go to my office.“
At the entrance, I was greeted by Iosef and his military entourage of young officers.
”You are overstepping and interrupting a personal meeting between me and the President.“
”Valken has a point. The military needs to be on the same page on any changes.“
entradas.menu: ”Valken has a point. The military needs to be on the same page on any changes.“

entradas.text: Iosef checked his folder before looking at me.
A strong knock on the door was heard and the Chief of the Armed Forces; Valken Kruger walked in quickly with a frown.
We walked from corridor to corridor to reach the office. On the way, we were met with high ranking officers as well as privates. Every time one of these soldiers saw me, they stopped and saluted me.
”This must be something serious. Especially since you invited me here.“
entradas.menu: ”This must be something serious. Especially since you invited me here.“

entradas.text: ”Where is Valken? He usually partakes in all military meetings.“
entradas.menu: ”Where is Valken? He usually partakes in all military meetings.“

entradas.text: ”Valken is busy at the moment overseeing the defensive strategies against Rumburg.“
”It is important that you don't get misinformed on this matter. Valken has another agenda.“
When we finally arrived at Iosef's office, his entourage saluted us and left. He closed the door and took a seat.
”The situation with Rumburg is getting worse and our lack of funding in the military means that we would fight for survival in a war scenario.“
”The situation with Rumburg is getting worse and if it wasn't for our investments in the military, I would be even more concerned.“
”We are prepared for the worst aren't we, Iosef?“
entradas.menu: ”We are prepared for the worst aren't we, Iosef?“

entradas.text: ”Your tone doesn't inspire confidence in our defensive capabilities.“
entradas.menu: ”Your tone doesn't inspire confidence in our defensive capabilities.“

entradas.text: ”Our soldiers are surely better motivated than theirs. We will defend our country!“
entradas.menu: ”Our soldiers are surely better motivated than theirs. We will defend our country!“

entradas.text: ”What are our options in improving the situation?“
entradas.menu: ”What are our options in improving the situation?“

entradas.text: ”Truthfully not fully prepared. We are still going through a few changes in the military to be able to confront them if such day was to arrive.“
”Our projected capability in the future should restore your confidence but we need to pass several changes to achieve a better situation.“
”Our efforts to restructure the military should prove beneficial in a potential conflict.“
”Since we refrained from modernising our military, the traditional force structure would have to match the enemies numbers.“

”We would never be able to match the force of Rumburg on equal terms therefore our switch of the military to a smaller, well-equipped and autonomously led combat units will prove better in the field.“
”You have been doing a fantastic job, Iosef. The military is in good hands.“
entradas.menu: ”You have been doing a fantastic job, Iosef. The military is in good hands.“

entradas.text: ”I trust that you will defend the country if it comes to the worst.“
entradas.menu: ”I trust that you will defend the country if it comes to the worst.“

entradas.text: ”Rumburg has superior numbers which we can't ever hope to match. The terrain is in our favour but once we cram hundreds of thousands in the mountains logistics will collapse.“
”The mandatory conscription law has become a matter of discussion and we need to strike a decision whether to keep it or remove it.“
Iosef cleared his throat.
”Whatever is necessary for our survival will be done when the time comes.“
entradas.menu: ”Whatever is necessary for our survival will be done when the time comes.“

entradas.text: ”Isn't Valken the supporter of the quantity over quality approach?“
entradas.menu: ”Isn't Valken the supporter of the quantity over quality approach?“

entradas.text: ”Why haven't I been invited? What is going on here?“
”There is no question in the motivation of our armed forces. However we must rely on the reality of the situation, especially when it is a matter of national survival.“
”We are making all the necessary preparations but any substantial military support from other nations would be a welcome deterrent against Rumburg.“
”Throwing bodies at a problem never solved it. Not sure if this is the right approach.“
entradas.menu: ”Throwing bodies at a problem never solved it. Not sure if this is the right approach.“

entradas.text: ”This doctrine worked for decades so far, no reason to change it. I think the generals have a point.“
entradas.menu: ”This doctrine worked for decades so far, no reason to change it. I think the generals have a point.“

entradas.text: ”I am doing my best to defend the country. There is nothing I care for more than Sordland.“
”Let's hope it doesn't come to that.“
”We have never failed to defend this nation from invaders. We won't start now.“
”With no disrespect to him but he thinks that you can outgun the enemy but when fighting a larger force outsmarting them is what matters.“
”It is the last step remaining to switch to a modern professional armed force.“
”Remove mandatory conscription. It is time to have a professional force of willingly enlisted soldiers.“
entradas.menu: ”Remove mandatory conscription. It is time to have a professional force of willingly enlisted soldiers.“

entradas.text: ”Are reservists really that damaging to the professional armed forces?“
entradas.menu: ”Are reservists really that damaging to the professional armed forces?“

entradas.text: ”If they are a hindrance then we should remove mandatory conscription.“
entradas.menu: ”If they are a hindrance then we should remove mandatory conscription.“

entradas.text: ”It will be a bloodbath for both sides.“
”Keep mandatory conscription. We need every single able body to defend the nation.“
entradas.menu: ”Keep mandatory conscription. We need every single able body to defend the nation.“

entradas.text: ”Sure. The new changes will be implemented as you wish.“
”Mr. President, I thought I explained it. Please rethink-.“
”We need all of our resources concentrated on our efficient units that will outperform the enemy in our mountainous terrain.“
”To truly modernise our fighting force we need to rid ourselves of the sluggish and inefficient cadets thrown to the ranks.“
”Well we can't have less troops on the front-line than the enemy. Not with our current structure focused on mass mobilisation.“
”I agree any huge structural change would be too late and too little now.“
”The choice is up to you.“
”I mean no disrespect but I am leading the ground operations and I must be informed of any strategic changes.“
”Well. Now that you are here, what is your opinion on conscription?“
entradas.menu: ”Well. Now that you are here, what is your opinion on conscription?“

entradas.text: ”Our restructuring is hindered by a hundred thousands of cadets extending our logistics, slowing command structure and reducing the combat efficiency of our experienced units.“
”The Minister of Defense is your superior and so am I.“
entradas.menu: ”The Minister of Defense is your superior and so am I.“

entradas.text: ”Thank you, Mr. President. We are talking about our national defense which must be consulted among all staff.“
”To clarify, we would have brought the subject up with the General Staff and you.“
”It depends if this is the President's wish.“
Valken left with a hard salute.
”Please excuse us, General Kruger.“
entradas.menu: ”Please excuse us, General Kruger.“

entradas.text: ”Expand the Air Force. We need more planes for air superiority.“
entradas.menu: ”Expand the Air Force. We need more planes for air superiority.“

entradas.text: ”Expand the Army. We need more soldiers to defend our nation.“
entradas.menu: ”Expand the Army. We need more soldiers to defend our nation.“

entradas.text: ”Expand the Navy. We need to increase the amount of our ships.“
entradas.menu: ”Expand the Navy. We need to increase the amount of our ships.“

entradas.text: ”Modernise the Navy. We need a higher-tech navy.“
entradas.menu: ”Modernise the Navy. We need a higher-tech navy.“

entradas.text: ”Modernise the Army. We need better equipped soldiers.“
entradas.menu: ”Modernise the Army. We need better equipped soldiers.“

entradas.text: ”Modernise the Air Force. We need a better air force.“
entradas.menu: ”Modernise the Air Force. We need a better air force.“

entradas.text: ”I could take my leave.“
”Agreed. There is a place for reservists.“
entradas.menu: ”Agreed. There is a place for reservists.“

entradas.text: ”We don't share the same opinion. This is a modern age and requires a modern army.“
entradas.menu: ”We don't share the same opinion. This is a modern age and requires a modern army.“

entradas.text: ”The matter is rather simple from my point of view.“
”Our forces have undergone large structural changes changing the operational capabilities and tactics.“
”We kept to our traditional army doctrine. It is not devoid of disadvantages.“
I left the Ministry of Defense and returned to the Maroon Palace.
”However, at the end of the day Rumburg has a larger army, air-force and navy. Our conscripts will fill the much needed weaknesses we have.“
”We also have to decide how exactly we spend our additional remaining funds in the military.“
”Let me look over my documents to see if there is anything else of concern.“
”Alright. Then we can move on.“
”That settles it then.“
”Mr. President. But-.“
”I would ask you to consider.“
”I don't think it is wise to change course now.“
"Mr. President, we need to prioritize quality over quantity."
”Revert the removal of mandatory conscription. That is my final decision.“
entradas.menu: ”Revert the removal of mandatory conscription. That is my final decision.“

entradas.text: ”No. I am content with the decision.“
entradas.menu: ”No. I am content with the decision.“

entradas.text: ”In June we decided to upgrade the equipment of our military.“
”The military thanks the administration for the extensive support.“
”In June we decided to expand the military.“
”We need to decide what branch we would want to expand further.“
”The military thanks the administration for the extensive support especially in creating a modern fighting force.“
”Which branch requires the expansion the most?“
entradas.menu: ”Which branch requires the expansion the most?“

entradas.text: ”The Army can be enlarged and match the force size of most neighbours.“
entradas.menu: ”The Army could be enlarged and match the force size of most neighbours.“

entradas.text: ”Which branch should we expand?“
”Strategically speaking the army would be the safest choice. However, the air and naval forces would do well with expansion too.“
”As you wish. The changes will be implemented this month and finished at the end of November.“
”Thank you for listening.“
”Each branch would give us an advantage. Our military is larger overall but we can expand the Army, Air Force or Navy even further.“
”The Air Force expansion could give us the battlefield advantage.“
entradas.menu: ”The Air Force expansion could give us the battlefield advantage.“

entradas.text: ”The Air Force would welcome the addition of new fighters and bombers. The air is the new front.“
”The Navy expansion could protect us from a possible naval incursion.“
entradas.menu: ”The Navy expansion could protect us from a possible naval incursion.“

entradas.text: ”Our nation has a long coast any naval expansion would protect our sea zone.“
”That's about it. I won't take more of your time sir.“
”Have a good day.“
entradas.menu: ”Have a good day.“

entradas.text: ”Thank you for your time.“
entradas.menu: ”Thank you for your time.“

entradas.text: ”Strategically speaking the army would be the safest choice. However, the air and naval forces would do well with expansion too.“
”Which branch requires the expansion the most?“
entradas.menu: ”Which branch requires the expansion the most?“

entradas.text: ”The Air Force would welcome the addition of new fighters and bombers. The air is the new front.“
”The Army can be enlarged and match the force size of most neighbours.“
entradas.menu: ”The Army could be enlarged and match the force size of most neighbours.“

entradas.text: ”Our nation has a long coast any naval expansion would protect our sea zone.“
”The Navy expansion could protect us from a possible naval incursion.“
entradas.menu: ”The Navy expansion could protect us from a possible naval incursion.“

entradas.text: ”The Air Force expansion could give us the battlefield advantage.“
entradas.menu: ”The Air Force expansion could give us the battlefield advantage.“

entradas.text: ”We need to decide what branch we would want to expand.“
”We need to decide what branch we would want to modernise more.“

”Our nation has a long coast, a naval modernisation would protect our sea zone. This would be important, especially now that the Heljiland situation between Agnolia and Valgsland is likely to escalate.“
”The Air Force would welcome the addition of modern fighters and bombers. The air is the new front.“
”Which branch requires the modernisation the most?“
entradas.menu: ”Which branch requires the modernisation the most?“

entradas.text: ”Strategically speaking the army would be the safest choice. However, the air and naval forces would do well with further modernisation too.“
”The Navy modernisation could protect us from a possible naval incursion through early detection.“
entradas.menu: ”The Navy modernisation could protect us from a possible naval incursion.“

entradas.text: ”The Air Force modernisation could give us the battlefield advantage through higher accuracy.“
entradas.menu: ”The Air Force modernisation could give us the battlefield advantage.“

entradas.text: ”The Army could be modernised and match the quality of most neighbours.“
entradas.menu: ”The Army could be modernised and match the quality of most neighbours.“

entradas.text: ”Which branch should we modernize?“
I left the Ministry of Defense and returned to the Maroon Palace.
I arrived at the cubic building that housed most of the military command that resided in Holsord. The grey and brutalist structure looked daunting.

I never liked this building. It always made me feel like I was standing under the concrete foot of a giant getting ready to crush me. It made me feel small and I never quite got used to the feeling even after this many years.
”Let's begin. What is the matter?“
entradas.menu: ”Let's begin. What is the matter?“

entradas.text: He leaned back and interlocked his hands.
”I will make sure it won't come to that.“
entradas.menu: ”I will make sure it won't come to that.“

entradas.text: ”Not everything might be up to us, sir.“
”Not everything might be up to us, sir.“
”I will make sure it won't come to that.“
entradas.menu: ”I will make sure it won't come to that.“

entradas.text: ”The recent military partnership we have signed with Agnolia includes a mutual-defense clause.“
”In case of conflict we will be obliged to come to each others aid. In case of a Rumburg invasion, they will come for help.“
”Do you think their support would be enough to hold the line?“
entradas.menu: ”Do you think their support would be enough to hold the line?“

entradas.text: ”I don't think so.“
”These are challenging times for us. Rumburg is a vulture circling around the region.“
”It is a disgrace that we have to rely on other nations for our defense.“
entradas.menu: ”It is a disgrace that we have to rely on other nations for our defense.“

entradas.text: ”Mr. President, we need stronger allies.“
”Sure, Agnolia is better than nothing but we must look further. Lespia or Valgsland are options in my opinion.“
”Any deterrence should force them to think twice.“
”Do you really think that is absolutely necessary?“
entradas.menu: ”Do you really think that is absolutely necessary?“

entradas.text: ”Advice noted. I will bring it up to Deivid.“
entradas.menu: ”Advice noted. I will bring it up to Deivid.“

entradas.text: ”Yes, it is. The danger far outweighs the sacrifice.“
”Sordland stands alone as always, Iosef. We won't rely on help from anyone else.“
entradas.menu: ”Sordland stands alone as always, Iosef. We won't rely on help from anyone else.“

entradas.text: ”I think the same way however, I am tasked with our nations defense. We need to look at the situation realistically.“
”I'd rather prevent a war altogether.“
entradas.menu: ”I'd rather prevent a war altogether.“

entradas.text: ”Me too but we might not have a choice.“
”I'd rather prevent a war altogether.“
entradas.menu: ”I'd rather prevent a war altogether.“

entradas.text: ”Me too but we might not have a choice.“
”Let's wait for Valken before we make a decision. I wanna hear his viewpoint.“
entradas.menu: ”Let's wait for Valken before we make a decision. I wanna hear his viewpoint.“

entradas.text: ”Mr. President, I don't think that will be necessary. He won't be comi-“
I thought for a moment before making my decision.
”What is the meaning of this?! Iosef?“
Valken deliberated the situation.
”I see what is going on here.“
”Disappointing. So this is how the administration conducts matters on military affairs.“
Valken looked furiously in my eyes.
”You heard your superior, Iosef.“
”As you wish, Mr. President.“
Iosef threw an angry look at Valken before turning to me.
I saluted and Iosef saluted back.
entradas.menu: Salute.

entradas.text: I saluted. Valken and Iosef saluted back.
entradas.menu: Salute.

entradas.text: ”Have a good day.“
entradas.menu: ”Have a good day.“

entradas.text: ”Thank you for your time.“
entradas.menu: ”Thank you for your time.“

entradas.text: ”The Kruger fortification line in construction should help us in the defense of the mountainous and hilly provinces and at the worst case delay a potential advance.“
”As a result of the recent deal with Wehlen, we have started reinforcing the border.“
”Forward scouts have been deployed and we have started moving our divisions.“
”Rest assured. We are ready for anything that will come from the other side of the border.“
”We will be providing our reports to you.“
”I don't think we will have any problems but stay alert. We don't know what we are dealing with yet.“
entradas.menu: ”I don't think we will have any problems but stay alert. We don't know what we are dealing with yet.“

entradas.text: ”I don't want anyone in. Do not let a single deserter pass our borders.“
entradas.menu: ”I don't want anyone in. Do not let a single deserter pass our borders.“

entradas.text: ”Try to be lenient if possible. There might be people who are simply trying to escape war among them.“
entradas.menu: ”Try to be lenient if possible. There might be people who are simply trying to escape war among them.“

entradas.text: ”We are always ready for any situation, Mr. President.“
”We won't, Mr. President.“
”We will try, Mr. President.“
”As a result of the recent deal with Wehlen, we have started organising the troops for the joint operation.“
”General Valken and I were discussing the war plan.“
”12th battalion of the 3rd Army, along with air support units, will do the job.“
”We will meet up with the Wehzek military command to discuss our joint strategy.“
”Excellent. I will be waiting for the results.“
entradas.menu: ”Excellent. I will be waiting for the results.“

entradas.text: ”Show them the might of the Sordish Armed Forces.“
entradas.menu: ”Show them the might of the Sordish Armed Forces.“

entradas.text: ”Be wary. I don't trust Wiktor Smolak even a little bit, nor his army.“
entradas.menu: ”Be wary. I don't trust Wiktor Smolak even a little bit, nor his army.“

entradas.text: ”You will be provided with our reports.“
”We are always ready for any situation, Mr. President.“
”The entire world will see, Mr. President. Don't doubt it.“
”Let's move on to our main topic.“
”Remove mandatory conscription. It is time to have a professional force of willingly enlisted soldiers.“
entradas.menu: ”Remove mandatory conscription. It is time to have a professional force of willingly enlisted soldiers.“

entradas.text: ”Keep mandatory conscription. We need every single able body to defend the nation.“
entradas.menu: ”Keep mandatory conscription. We need every single able body to defend the nation.“

entradas.text: ”The facts are that the conscription gives us a large reservist pool that can cover a larger frontline but these troops lack the morale and quality to be offensive elements.“
”My argument would be to remove conscription if our military can stand on it's own two feet without them. If we are going to have strong allies why do we need conscripts?“
”You can stay, Valken.“
entradas.menu: ”You can stay, Valken.“

entradas.text: "Your final decision, Mr. President."
”Please leave us to conduct the meeting in private, Valken.“
entradas.menu: ”Please leave us to conduct the meeting in private, Valken.“

entradas.text: ”Tell me what you think, General Kruger.“
entradas.menu: ”Tell me what you think, General Kruger.“
